diagnoses.label: identifier-redaction patterns incomplete (arXiv/DOI/URL variants)
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Verifier: ::test_identifiers_redacted failed while ::test_authors_redacted and ::test_affiliations_redacted passed, indicating identity leakage remains specifically via identifiers rather than names/affiliations.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: When anonymizing academic papers for blind review, enumerate and target non-name identity leaks (arXiv IDs, DOIs, URLs, submission/accepted venue strings, preprint footers) in addition to names/affiliations.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Non-academic PDFs or tasks where identifiers are intentionally preserved (e.g., bibliographic archiving, citation indexing).
diagnoses.recommended_direction: Expand the identifier category beyond the single arXiv/DOI examples to include common real-world variants (case/spacing/prefix differences, URL forms like arxiv.org/abs/, dx.doi.org/, doi.org/, and other repository identifiers) and explicitly instruct collecting these strings from the document text/metadata before redaction.

diagnoses.label: content-preservation guardrail not operational (no post-redaction retention check in main flow)
diagnoses.observable_evidence: ::test_content_preserved failed while ::test_structural_integrity passed, suggesting the output remains a valid PDF but too much textual content was removed/obscured; the skill mentions “Check that 80%+ of original text remains” and provides verify_redaction(), but this is guidance-only and not integrated as a required step with clear thresholds/stop conditions.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Any PDF redaction operation where the goal is anonymization while preserving the paper’s readable content and layout.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Workflows intentionally removing large portions of content (e.g., summarization by extraction, heavy censorship, page-level removal).
diagnoses.recommended_direction: Strengthen the verification mechanism into a mandatory, stepwise gate: define explicit retained-text thresholds (and what to do when failing), require counting redaction annotations applied, and require spot-checking that only matched rectangles were redacted; tie these checks to iteration (tighten patterns / reduce overbroad matches) before saving final outputs.

diagnoses.label: references boundary detection ambiguous causing over-redaction
diagnoses.observable_evidence: ::test_self_citations_preserved passed but ::test_content_preserved failed; the skill’s stop condition is a simplistic “if 'references' in page text” which can mis-detect (e.g., 'References' in headers/TOC/footers) and lead to redaction being applied too widely or skipped inconsistently, impacting overall content retention.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Determining where to stop redacting (main text/front matter) and where to preserve (References and beyond) in academic PDFs.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Documents without a References section or with radically different structure (slides, posters, brochures).
diagnoses.recommended_direction: Clarify and harden the boundary rule: require robust detection (e.g., first occurrence of a standalone 'References' heading with typography/position heuristics, or confirming subsequent citation-like patterns), and add a fallback manual/visual check when detection is uncertain to prevent unnecessary redactions that harm content preservation.

overlay.composition_issue: Identifier leakage persists because the enumeration/pattern set is incomplete, while content loss indicates the redaction application and boundary detection can be overbroad; expanding identifier coverage must be coupled with stricter verification gates and clearer stop-redacting boundaries to avoid worsening content preservation.
preservation_constraints: Preserve the rule to not redact the References section so self-citations remain intact
Preserve the guidance to redact only specific search matches (not whole-page/region redaction)
Preserve structural integrity checks (page count should not change)

package_assessment.rationale: All observed failures are attributable to modifiable, reusable-skill guidance mechanisms (identifier enumeration/pattern coverage, boundary detection guidance, and verification gating) localized to academic-pdf-redaction/SKILL.md without needing changes to external systems.
